t.6.110.1: Seeing that Puṣpaka, adorned with flowers, arrived and standing close by, Vibhīṣaṇa addressed Rāma.
t.6.110.2: But he, the lord of the rākṣasas, with palms joined in reverence, bowing low and humble, and filled with eagerness, said to Rāghava, "What shall I do?"
t.6.110.3: Having reflected, the greatly splendid Rāghava spoke to him these words, prompted by affection, while Lakṣmaṇa listened.
t.6.110.4: O Vibhīṣaṇa, honour the forest-dwellers, who have accomplished their deeds with great effort, with jewels, with wealth, and with ornaments of many kinds.
t.6.110.5: O lord of the rākṣasas, it was with these, joyful and never turning back in battle, casting aside all fear for their lives, that Laṅkā was harried and conquered.
t.6.110.6: O giver of honour, these leaders of the monkey troops, who are worthy of honour, will be content when they are thus honoured by you, who are grateful.
t.6.110.8: Thus addressed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa honored all those monkeys, distributing among them jewels and riches.
t.6.110.7: Because people know you to be generous, one who wins and holds people to himself, compassionate and illustrious, therefore I counsel you.
t.6.110.10: Taking upon his lap the glorious Vaidehī, who was abashed, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, valiant and bearing a bow,
t.6.110.9: Then, seeing those troop-leaders honored with jewels and riches, the far-renowned Rāma ascended that unsurpassed aerial chariot.
t.6.110.11: And Kākutstha, standing in the aerial chariot, spoke to all the monkeys, to the mighty Sugrīva, and to the rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.110.12: O best of the vānaras, this task of a friend has been accomplished by you. You are all given leave by me; return as you wish.
t.6.110.13: Whatever a companion or a friend ought to do, O Sugrīva, scorcher of foes, all that has been done by you, who fear to stray from dharma. Return quickly to Kiṣkindhā, surrounded by your own army.
t.6.110.14: O Vibhīṣaṇa, dwell in Laṅkā, in your own kingdom given to you by me. Not even the heaven-dwellers together with Indra are able to assail you.
t.6.110.15: I shall return to Ayodhyā, the royal capital of my father. I wish to be given leave; I bid farewell to all of you.
t.6.110.16: Thus addressed by Rāma, those mighty vānaras, and the rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa too, spoke to Rāma with joined palms: "We wish to go to Ayodhyā; may your honour lead us all there."
t.6.110.17: Having seen you still moist from the consecration and having paid our respects to Kausalyā, we shall soon return to our own homes, O son of the king.
t.6.110.18: Thus addressed by the monkeys together with Vibhīṣaṇa, the righteous-souled and glorious Rāghava spoke to them, along with Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.110.19: It will be a gain dearer than the dearest that I, with my friends and accompanied by all of you, shall find joy on reaching the city.
t.6.110.20: Quickly board the aerial chariot, O Sugrīva, together with the monkeys; and you too, O Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, ascend it along with your ministers.
t.6.110.21: Then Sugrīva, together with his army, hastening, quickly ascended that divine Puṣpaka, and so did Vibhīṣaṇa with his ministers.
t.6.110.22: When they had all climbed aboard, the supreme seat of Kubera, permitted by Rāghava, flew up into the sky.
t.6.110.23: He went forth in that radiant aerial car yoked with swans; and Rāma, delighted and joyful, shone like Kubera.
